structured.answer: Keren hishtalmut is a savings account from my salary: the employer adds up to 7.5% and I add 2.5%. The profits are tax-free if I wait 6 years from the first payment; I can take it out earlier but then it's taxed. Worth keeping, mainly because the employer puts money in, though the page's own comparison showed only about 415 ₪ more after 10 years, which confused me.

stuck.why: Made the keren look barely better than a securities account; only later noticed the employer's money is 'מחוץ להשוואה', and I'm not sure I understood that
Minus sign means it could come out worse? Scared me, didn't understand why
Don't know if that's a lot; no shekel figure for it

findings.what: The headline comparison shows only 415.84 ₪ more for the keren, which makes it look barely worth it; the employer's 7.5% is left out and that's only mentioned in small text
A range with a minus sign (-342.02 ₪) scares me without explaining
The '6 שנים' point is repeated in about five places; it gets tiring
Every block has the same 'חוקים וכללים · N' chip; I stopped noticing them
Fees only in percent ('עד 2% בשנה'), no shekel amount
Lots of jargon (הפקדה מוטבת, ריאלי, ותק, משכורת קובעת)
